findings.evidence: The Act is at 23 Stat. 103. Source credit of former 43 U.S.C. 1071: 'act July 5, 1884, ch. 214, sec. 1, 23 Stat. 103' (law.justia.com 1999 U.S. Code, 43 U.S.C. 1071). findings.claim: date_rule fixed 1930-04-01, 'last day of the 91-day preference period beginning on the 63rd day after December 31, 1929'.
findings.evidence: EO 5254 (held, jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-5254-...txt) opens the land to ex-servicemen 'for a period of 91 days beginning with the 63rd day from and after the date hereof' (December 31, 1929). The 63rd day after Dec. 31, 1929 is March 4, 1930 (31 days of January + 28 of February = 59; March 4 = 63rd); 91 days beginning March 4 end June 2, 1930. The branch's own basis sentence and the .md both say June 2, 1930; only the machine date is wrong, so every lead the engine writes for EO 5254 carries 1930-04-01.
findings.fix: Set the B09 fixed date to 1930-06-02.

findings.location: procedure B20 (lead.basis, date_rule.to 1947-03-26); mechanism M4; source S-MBA1947 'establishes'; .md (a) M4 'the agreement retained only the listed bases'
findings.claim: A Philippine reservation at a place not listed in Annex A or B was surrendered on July 4, 1946 (Army) or no later than March 26, 1947, because the 1947 agreement retained only the listed bases.
findings.evidence: Military Bases Agreement of March 14, 1947 (UNTS No. 673, read on the web at treaties.un.org) art. XXI(1): 'the United States shall retain the right to occupy temporary quarters and installations now existing outside the bases mentioned in Annex A and Annex B for such reasonable time, not exceeding two years' (extension by mutual agreement, excluded for the City of Manila, 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years'); art. XXI(2): 'the Port of Manila reservation with boundaries as of 1941 will be available for use to the United States armed forces until such time as other arrangements can be made'; art. XXI(3) gives the United States 'full use and full control' of those quarters while occupied. So the agreement, which Art. I of the Treaty of General Relations makes the measure of what was retained, kept U.S. use of non-listed installations beyond March 26, 1947 and of the Manila Port Reservation with no fixed end. Under ruling P5 such members need the instrument disposing of the excepted property or the upper bound the last instrument fixes. B20 decides as `no` by 1947-03-26 the Port Reservation orders EO 1298 (Manila, incl. the Port Reservation), EO 2838 (enlarging the Port Reservation), EO 3344 and EO 3500 ('Port Reservation' modified/enlarged), EO 348A (reclaimed harbor land, Manila) and probably EO 5736 (lands in Manila Harbor) and EO 4787 (Manila lands).
findings.fix: Quote art. XXI in S-MBA1947 and M4. Move Port of Manila reservation members (at least EO 1298, 2838, 3344, 3500, 348A; check EO 5736, 4787, 964) to an open branch (need the instrument ending U.S. use of the Port reservation). For the remaining B20 members either show from a source that the installation was not occupied as temporary quarters after March 26, 1947, or widen the interval's upper bound to the art. XXI limit (1949-03-26, or at most three years, 1950-03-26) and disclose that the exact date depends on occupation. Drop 'retained only the listed bases' and the flat 'July 4, 1946 for Army reservations'.

findings.location: branches C07 (EO 5174) and C16 (EO 456) versus ruling P2 and branch B10m
findings.claim: EO 5174 and EO 456 end on the date of the later order that revoked or rescinded them (1929-12-14; 1907-05-16).
findings.evidence: EO 5174 only amends EO 4679 (WPA summary 'E. O. 4679 ... amended to correct description') and EO 456 only amends EO 372-B. Ruling P2 says an order whose only content is an amendment merges into the parent on issue, kind merged_into_parent_on_issue, dated by the amending order's own date, with the stated disclosure. The doctrine applies P2 to six other amending orders (B10m) but not to these two.
findings.fix: Either apply P2 to EO 5174 and EO 456 (date 1929-08-21 and 1906-06-08, with the P2 disclosure) and record the later revocation as a later event of the parent, or state why the later revocation governs for these two.

summary: The doctrine's structure and most of its sources hold up. All 29 held sources match their sha256 and pin, and each of the 25 later orders behind branches C01-C25 names its target as the branch says. The 1934 Act, Proclamation 2695, FLPMA and the Panama Canal Act pages are cited correctly, and the branch counts (143 no, 173 open) reproduce. Five errors need fixing. The 1884 Act is cited as 23 Stat. 130 instead of 23 Stat. 103. The B09 machine date for EO 5254 is 1930-04-01; the order's 91-day period ends 1930-06-02. The B20 upper bound of 1947-03-26 ignores art. XXI of the 1947 Military Bases Agreement, which let U.S. forces keep temporary installations for up to two or three years and keep the Port of Manila reservation until other arrangements were made, so the Port Reservation members (EO 1298, 2838, 3344, 3500, 348A) are wrongly decided `no`. The .md says the engine reports no contradictions, but the engine reports 23. And the undecided list says no end can be shown from the fields held, while held edges name revocations for about 23 open members (14 PLO revocations on B33, EO 432 for EO 330-A, EO 4716 for EO 4671, seven on B31), including EO 1450, which the doctrine cites as possibly still standing. The minor points are a misrouted relinquishment (EO 3402), EO 2879 left open although it appears fully relinquished, two false edges to disclose, P2 applied inconsistently to EO 5174 and EO 456, and an overstated PCA 'establishes' sentence.
